text:
mira: seeing a ~28% p95 throughput drop on nf4 canary compared to baseline starting at 03:12 UTC. rolling threshold hit for >256 seq workloads.

aj: ugh, same graphs here. p50 roughly stable, p95 and p99 blow up. can you paste the profiler traces?

mira: pasted key slice from perf_profile:
```
kernel_select: nf4_opt_v2 -> nf4_slowpath
batching: adaptive_batcher size jumped from 512->1536 for some traces
kv_cache: eviction spikes + write amplification
latency_breakdown: aten_kernel_wait + kernel_dispatch_queue + memcpy_host2dev
```

kyle: that kernel_select transition looks suspicious. nf4_slowpath has extra quant-dequant steps we hoped to avoid. was there a recent kernel metadata change?

mira: yes, runtime rolled nf4_opt_v2 metadata last night (PR #4123) to add better accuracy guards. probably the guard triggered and fell back to slowpath.

aj: who approved the guard? @kyle?

kyle: I did the PR but only changed a metadata flag. didn't expect it to cause fallback in prod. immediate mitigation: can we pin the canary model to nf4_opt_v1 while we investigate?

sam: deploy-bot: pinned model:search/nf4-2026-03 to kernel_profile=nf4_opt_v1 on canary cluster c-17 :white_check_mark:

mira: thank you. after pinning throughput climbed back ~+25% to previous baseline in canary within 3 minutes.

devin: looking at KV cache telemetry — eviction rate jumped x5 right after the guard started hitting. Memory RSS per worker rose from 6.8GB -> 9.3GB before OOMs, because slowpath allocates a transient buffer for quant calibration.

aj: this explains the memory spikes. why would batching jump? is adaptive_batcher using latency hist windows that got noisy due to kernel jitter and therefore increased target batch to saturate throughput?

mira: exactly. adaptive_batcher saw higher variance and increased allowed batch tokens to keep throughput, but that pushed transient memory over threshold and triggered evictions. Evictions then invalidated prefix cache and increased compute. bad feedback loop.

sam: short checklist of actions: 1) keep canary pinned to nf4_opt_v1 2) revert metadata flag in staging 3) add guard in adaptive_batcher to cap max_batch_tokens=1024 for nf4 paths 4) add telemetry counter for kernel_fallback_reason.

kyle: I'll open a revert PR for the metadata flag (WIP: #4188).

mira: adding a lightweight hotfix: runtime health rule to throttle new long-seq requests when mem_usage > 80% on a worker. devin can you add a KV eviction backoff?

devin: yes, implementing eviction backoff: when eviction_rate > 2x baseline, reduce batch size by 25% and enable aggressive prefix reuse. rolling patch in review.

aj: what about a longer-term fix?

kyle: long-term: we need a smarter kernel selector that takes transient mem footprint into account (not just latency) and a simulation harness to validate metadata flag impact on kernel selection. also calibrate slowpath alloc pattern to pre-allocate pooling instead of per-request allocations.

mira: also want more granular telemetry: include kernel_id in trace spans and add a sampled stack for slowpath entries so we can see which inputs trigger fallback.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-094, assigned to eng-runtime. priority P2.

sam: plan for today: deploy pin -> monitor canary for 30m -> revert metadata in staging -> land batch cap + eviction backoff. communicate to infra and support.

aj: thanks team. please add any immediate numbers to the incident doc. I'll coordinate customer comms if we see broader impact. :thumbsup:
